question: which typed fields have enough repeated transitions to support a constant step, and what does requiring that cost?

rule.declaredBefore: committed before any S11A run on a real cartridge
rule.statement: at least two observed transitions whose non-zero steps agree
rule.onFailure: INSUFFICIENT_TRANSITION_SUPPORT: the candidate is kept with its measurements for diagnosis; this is a statement about the evidence, NOT about the field being useless

scoring: false typings AND lost useful candidates, counted separately. A drop in the number of typed fields is not by itself a success
armControl: legacy typing (transitionSupport off) is the control; FIRST-V1 and the pipeline are untouched
oracleDiscipline: opened only after both arms have typed the cartridge

firstEventBlindness.defect: the typing stage samples RAM only AFTER each observed event, so a change that happens during the FIRST event and never again has nothing to be compared against and is invisible to typing
firstEventBlindness.where: play() in agod-pipeline.js, and the same schedule reproduced here
firstEventBlindness.consequence: part of the single-transition population the transition-support rule is meant to judge never reaches typing at all, so neither arm can see it
firstEventBlindness.foundBy: the single-transition fixture typed neither of its labelled cases until an arming delay was added to move their transition inside the sampled window
firstEventBlindness.note: not fixed in this stage: changing when typing samples is a change to the typer and belongs to its own declared stage

totals.note: a fall in typedByRule is not a success on its own; read falseTypings against lostUsefulCandidates
